subject: Chemistry
description: He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn — properties, uses, electronic configuration, discovery

questions.stem: NOBLE GASES are characterised by being chemically:

options.option_text: Highly reactive with most metals usually
Largely inert due to a complete outer shell
Acidic in water at room temperature only
Toxic to humans and to plants in air

questions.explanation: Noble gases (Group 18) — He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn (+ synthetic Og). All have COMPLETE outer electron shell (He has 2; rest have 8). Hence chemically inert — don't readily form compounds. He never forms compounds. Other noble gases (Xe, Kr, Rn) form a few compounds with strong oxidisers (XeF₂, XeF₄, XeO₃) — discovered by Neil Bartlett 1962, breaking the assumption of total inertness. Distractor 1 — opposite. Distractor 3 — false. Distractor 4 — generally non-toxic, though radon is radioactive.

questions.stem: HELIUM is widely used in airships and weather balloons because it is:

options.option_text: The lightest gas, hydrogen, easily combustible
Less dense than air but non-flammable, unlike H₂
Heavier than air and gives stable downward lift
Coloured pink and gives an attractive appearance

questions.explanation: Helium — second-lightest gas (after H₂). Density ~0.18 g/L (vs air 1.2 g/L). NON-FLAMMABLE, unlike hydrogen (which caused the Hindenburg disaster, 1937). Used in airships, blimps, weather balloons, party balloons. Other uses: cryogenic cooling (LHe at 4K, for MRI superconducting magnets), purging rocket-fuel tanks, deep-sea breathing mix (heliox — replaces nitrogen to avoid bends). Distractor 1 — He is gas #2, lighter than only H₂. Distractor 3 — He is much LESS dense than air. Distractor 4 — colourless.

questions.stem: The reddish-orange glow of NEON SIGNS is produced by:

options.option_text: Burning the neon gas with oxygen in tubes
Electric current exciting neon atoms to emit light
Reflecting external red light off coloured glass
Neon gas heated until it gets red-hot

questions.explanation: Neon sign — high-voltage electrical discharge through low-pressure neon gas excites atoms; on returning to ground state, they emit characteristic reddish-orange light (~640 nm). Different colours in 'neon' signs come from different gases or coated glass — argon (blue/lavender), krypton (greenish white), xenon (blue-violet), helium (pink), Hg + phosphor (white, blue, green). Genuine neon-only signs are red-orange. Distractor 1 — noble gases don't burn. Distractor 3 — they self-emit. Distractor 4 — incandescence not the mechanism.

questions.stem: ARGON is used to fill ELECTRIC LIGHT BULBS because it:

options.option_text: Reacts with the tungsten filament to extend life
Is inert, preventing oxidation of the hot filament
Lights up itself, giving extra brightness inside
Cools the filament rapidly during operation

questions.explanation: Tungsten filament gets hot (~2500-3000°C). In air, it would oxidise + burn quickly. Filling the bulb with INERT GAS (Ar, sometimes Kr/Xe for premium bulbs) prevents oxidation, extends bulb life. Argon is the cheapest noble gas (~1% of atmosphere). Some bulbs add nitrogen (also unreactive at these conditions). LED bulbs don't need this — solid-state, no hot filament. Distractor 1 — opposite. Distractor 3 — argon doesn't self-light. Distractor 4 — gases conduct some heat but cooling isn't the main reason.

questions.stem: RADON, the heaviest naturally-occurring noble gas, is a health concern because it is:

options.option_text: Highly explosive in confined spaces near homes
Radioactive and a major cause of lung cancer indoors
Toxic by direct contact with the human skin
Acidic when dissolved in indoor air moisture

questions.explanation: Radon (Rn-222, half-life 3.8 days) — radioactive decay product of uranium in soil + rock. Seeps into homes through foundations, accumulates in poorly-ventilated basements + ground floors. Inhaled radon decays into radioactive progeny that lodge in lungs → SECOND LEADING CAUSE OF LUNG CANCER after smoking (in many developed countries). Mitigation: sealing cracks, sub-slab ventilation. Common in granite-rich areas. Health limit: < 4 pCi/L typical. Distractor 1 — not explosive (inert). Distractor 3 — chemically inert; danger is radioactivity, not chemical contact. Distractor 4 — not acidic.

questions.stem: ARGON makes up approximately what percentage of Earth's atmosphere by volume?

options.option_text: 0.04%, like CO₂ in current atmosphere
0.93%, the third most abundant gas in air
21%, like the share of oxygen in air
78%, like the nitrogen content in air

questions.explanation: Atmosphere composition (dry air, by volume): N₂ 78.08%, O₂ 20.95%, ARGON 0.93%, CO₂ ~0.04% (and rising), Ne 0.0018%, He 0.00052%, Kr 0.00011%, H₂ 0.00005%, Xe 0.0000087%. Argon is the THIRD most abundant atmospheric gas (and most abundant noble gas). Distractor 1 = CO₂ level. Distractor 3 = O₂. Distractor 4 = N₂.

questions.stem: Helium-Neon (HeNe) lasers and Argon-ion lasers are examples of:

options.option_text: Solid-state lasers built from doped crystals
Gas lasers, with a noble gas as the lasing medium
Liquid lasers using dye solutions inside cells
Semiconductor lasers used in CD and DVD readers

questions.explanation: GAS LASERS — population inversion in gaseous medium under electric discharge. HeNe (632.8 nm red, classroom + barcode-scanner) — first continuous-wave laser, 1960. Argon-ion (488/514 nm blue-green, used in eye surgery, retinal photocoagulation, scientific research). CO₂ lasers (10.6 μm IR, used in industrial cutting, welding) are also gas lasers. Distractor 1 = ruby, Nd:YAG, Ti:sapphire (solid-state). Distractor 3 = dye lasers (tunable, used in research). Distractor 4 = laser diodes (small, efficient, ubiquitous in consumer electronics).
